name: AltText.ai
summary: Bulk AI alt-text generation for image-heavy sites: crawls your pages or plugs into your CMS (WordPress, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Contentful, DatoCMS) and writes the alt attributes back automatically, in 130+ languages.
best_for: image-heavy sites that need alt text written back into the CMS automatically: e-commerce catalogues, publishers and long-running blogs on WordPress, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, Contentful, DatoCMS or Storyblok. The native integrations, page crawler, CSV import/export and developer API let you clear thousands of missing alt attributes without touching them by hand
skip_if: you have a few dozen images. Write those yourself for free and you will describe them better than any model, because you know why each image is on the page. Also skip it if your visuals are diagram-, product- or brand-specific enough that every generated line needs rewriting anyway — in which case the credits buy you a draft you were going to redo
honest_knock: The headline ‘5¢ per image’ only holds for a plain JPG in one language. AVIF, HEIC, SVG and TIFF bill double — precisely the formats a performance-tuned image pipeline outputs — and every extra language adds another credit per image, so by the published rules one AVIF product shot in five languages is six credits, not one. Those advanced formats are also locked out of the 25-credit free trial, so the one thing you cannot measure before paying is your own burn rate. In our test on 20 October 2026 the free upload form refused an AVIF with 'Please choose a JPG, PNG, or WebP image.' before charging a credit, and plain JPG and PNG images cost 1 credit each. With English and Dutch both selected we got only a Dutch text for 1 credit, so check what a multi-language run returns before you budget for one. Credits are spent on generation rather than on acceptance: regenerate a line you didn’t like and you pay again, and AltText.ai states plainly that used credits are not normally refundable. The category caveat an honest review owes you: models describe what is visibly in a photo well, but alt text is a judgement call. Whether an image is decorative or informative, and what your brand actually calls the thing in it, is context the model doesn’t have. Bulk generation is a far better starting point than the empty alt attributes on most sites, but treat the output as a draft to spot-check. ‘ADA compliance’ here means the field gets filled, not a legal guarantee that what’s in it is right.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 10 Oct 2026; figures unchanged since 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image.

compare_with.name: accessiBe
compare_with.why: accessiBe is an accessibility overlay — a script that patches issues in the visitor’s browser at runtime. AltText.ai writes real alt text into your CMS, so it lives in your source, ships to every visitor and is what search crawlers actually read. Pick the overlay for broad WCAG patching across a site you cannot easily edit; pick AltText.ai when you specifically want durable alt text in the page itself

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the free account with 25 credits: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We uploaded our own simple 600x400 test images (a blue circle as JPG, PNG and AVIF, an orange square as PNG), asked for one in Dutch, and looked them up again in the library.
findings: Each image cost 1 credit: the blue circle as JPG, the circle as PNG and the orange square as PNG took the balance from 25 to 22.

The texts were correct and added nothing that was not there: 'A solid blue circle centered on a white background.' and 'An orange square centered on a white background.' The PNG of the circle gave exactly the same text as the JPG.

With Dutch added next to English (the language field says 'Credits: 1 per language'), only a Dutch text was saved, 'Een effen blauwe cirkel, gecentreerd op een witte achtergrond.' ('A solid blue circle, centred on a white background'), for 1 credit (22 to 21). This test does not settle how multi-language runs are billed.

The AVIF was refused in the upload form before anything ran: 'Please choose a JPG, PNG, or WebP image.' with 'Upgrade to support advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF)'. No credit was used. The upload label itself lists 'JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP, or BMP (max 16MB)'.
The library search looks in the alt text, not the Asset ID: 'TEST-A' gave 'Your search returned no results.', while 'blue circle' found the two English records of the circle (not the Dutch one).
The library listed all four records with Asset ID, source 'Direct Upload', text and time, but the edit page showed 'Image unavailable': the uploaded image itself is not shown again.
End state: 21 of 25 credits left after four generations and one refused AVIF.
